Other land use impacts would result from the construction of pipelines carrying water to the site and product delivery systems. Pipelines would be buried and land usage disturbance would be for a short period only.
Land use changes would also occur as the towns and community centers expand due to an influx of workers and their families. Presumably, the greatest effect would be in Hardin, where residential expansion would result in the loss of irrigated agricultural land in Big Horn Valley.
Sound - Since definite plans have not been developed for a conversion plant, noise effects of constructing this facility cannot be definitely described. It is assumed that construction of a plant would be during the day and occur simultaneously with coal development.
It is estimated that the equivalent sound level contribution, 1,000 feet from the center of a gasification plant construction site, would be 74 dB<sup>a</sup>, and that from the operation of a typical coal gasification plant and its associated facilities is estimated to be 48dB<sup>a</sup>, at 1,000 feet (Dames & Moore, 1976). It is assumed that plant operations would be continuous.
Aesthetics
The shaping or carving of the land by excavations and other visual disturbances associated with the development of the roads, power lines, and pipelines needed to support a conversion plant would create lines on the landscape in conflict with the natural lines of the terrain.
